correctness.rationale: PASS: Any automorphism of the Fraisse limit L restricts to a pointed isomorphism of <a>, and ultrahomogeneity extends a pointed isomorphism to Aut(L). Local finiteness makes <a> finite. For each n>=2 Nishimura gives a single finite n-element one-generated Heyting algebra Z_n. Citkin reports two distinguished generators for Z2,Z4,Z5 and unique generators for other Z_n; the pair in Z4 and Z5 is interchanged by an algebra automorphism, unlike Z2, whose 0 and 1 are named constants and must be fixed. Consequently there are exactly two singleton G-orbits, and one orbit for each n>=3. Strong amalgamation of the finite-Heyting age over the constants algebra constructs arbitrarily many disjoint generators of each n>=3 type, all realized in countable L, so every nonconstant orbit is countably infinite. The proof does not infer the infinite action from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: PASS: A full unary orbit profile of the natural non-oligomorphic automorphism action on the universal homogeneous Heyting algebra is a motivated structure theorem. It pinpoints the earliest arity of infinitely many orbits and sorts all singleton stabilizers by one-generated subalgebra size, useful for further oligomorphicity/stabilizer studies; this is more than restating the existence of infinitely many finite algebras.
